rules.title: California Civil Rights Council regulations on use of criminal history in housing
rules.requirement: Limits what criminal history a housing provider may seek, how it may be considered, and what actions may be taken based on it. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-record bans; arrests without conviction may not be considered
rules.interaction: Builds on 2016 HUD disparate-impact guidance; local criminal-history ordinances may add further limits.
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.

rules.title: SB 329 (2019): housing subsidies as protected source of income under FEHA
rules.requirement: FEHA's definition of 'source of income' includes government housing subsidy programs such as Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers; landlords may not refuse to participate in such programs or maintain 'No Section 8' policies.
rules.key_value: Source-of-income discrimination including Section 8 vouchers prohibited
rules.interaction: Enforced by the California Civil Rights Department.
rules.quoted_span: This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.

rules.title: SB 267 (2023): credit history limits for applicants with government rental subsidies
rules.requirement: Rental property owners may not use credit history in the application process for an applicant with a government rental subsidy (e.g., Section 8) without offering the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable lawful means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.key_value: Must offer alternative evidence option before using credit history for subsidized applicants
rules.quoted_span: to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.conflict_note: Document says 'last year's SB 267' in an article dated circa Sept. 2024 (per linked CRD announcement), implying 2023 enactment; effective date derived from CA default rule (Jan. 1 following chaptering).
